checks: Barycentric coordinates force a nonnegative integer vector to have sum at most one. A negative least coordinate -h forces -3h <= sum z_i <= 1-4h, hence h=1 and all three coordinates -1. Exact determinant computation gives tetrahedral volume 2/3.

The ordinary lower bound at the product centroid pairs the scalar symmetric noise from B and uses the accepted dimension-three paired tails. Pure B normals give 1/2, and zero continuous restriction keeps the whole fiber. Through-point barycentric cuts give the matching uniform upper bound 27/64.

The cyclic vertex map is an affine volume-preserving automorphism of the tetrahedron. It is linear because the centroid is zero, and its four rotated x vectors sum to zero; paired signs of W cancel. Each outer marginal is uniform, and the zero-sum coupling guarantees at least one closed cap membership including ties.

A large finite base tilt includes exactly one outer fiber for the middle-fiber upper test, and the exposed outer-site version isolates only its own trace. Thus the maximum is (1+27/64)/5=91/320 and the four outer bases are strictly below it. Exact rational checks reproduced support, determinants and constants.
